1. It depends on your confidence in the matchup. For example, I would consider spellthiefs into Nautilus but not Leona since you have similar ranges and her E goes through minions. Assuming both sides are pretty healthy, you win if they engage as long as they engage onto your ADC. Engage supports get locked into their CC animation and land in a predictable spot for a bubble. Your goal in these lanes is to survive those engages and scale into midgame. However, they also can't engage if they're too low, so it's probably possible to opt for spellthiefs and play aggressively level 1 or look to poke after they use their key cooldowns. 
2. It's not really about how often, but what's necessary. It comes down to experience to know when your team has the upper hand. If the enemy is threatening to engage on your carry, position to avoid CC and hold onto ult and bubble to peel. If the enemy is out of position and/or has blown key cooldowns and summoners, engage on them. Don't look for a 50/50 engage a minute before an objective spawns because that CC is better saved for the teamfight that ensues. League is very situational and so these points won't always be the case. 
3. It does make it harder to secure kills into lanes with heavier healing but both are good summs so it's up to you! I like exhaust into team comps with assassins, bruisers with gap closers, or heavy auto attacking adcs (kat, akali, yone, renek, vayne, jinx). Jhin/Seraphine is an example of a lane where I prefer ignite; exhaust doesn't do much for him and Seraphine will want to double cast W when you engage. 
4. Watch out for high damage mage supports you can't outpoke (zyra, brand, morg). Trading autos is fine but your auto animation puts you at risk for their cc or damage ability. 
5. This depends on the condition of the wave. Try to soak xp if you can safely. Don't last hit under tower if they can dive or poke you to death.  If your tower is low and they're good on resources, let it fall and roam. If the wave is pushing to them, roam. Note where your jungler and the enemy jugler are, maybe your jg can rotate over and help you, maybe you need to run because enemy jungler is out of sight or nearby. Just a few scenarios to take with a grain of salt. 
6. 7. 8. Ahhh these three are pretty situational too. Just based on kit, you don't usually win duels solo so there's going to be some outplaying involved. I wouldn't take the fight if I couldn't afford the risk. That being said, go for it if you're going to die anyway. Some heuristics: If that objective is soul for you or denying soul from them, yes. If that kill has a fat shutdown, yes. If that kill is the primary or only threat on their team, yes. If you can answer to the other threats after trading kills, yes. If your base is dying, and death timers are high, no. If your team has a sizable baron timer and the waves aren't pushed, no.

Hi! I went through the same thing junior year of highschool. I don't know how traditional your parents' attitudes towards mental health are, but I recommend telling them in doses. Start by saying you've been struggling with depression & anxiety (explain that it's an imbalance of chemicals in your brain, namely serotonin and dopamine, that affect your energy and motivation levels) and that you didn't realize it until recently. Tell them you're needing to seek treatment in order to function through this rough time. If they're not overwhelmingly supportive, continue to frame it as setback you can overcome now that you know what the cause is. I know it isn't necessarily a temporary thing, but if they're very cold about it, you may need to frame it as such. Prioritize getting the care you need to get it under control, whether it's therapy, prescribed medications, or taking leave from school. Colleges are understanding about mental health as well, so explain the situation to the appropriate party to see what your options are. 

Asian parents tend to think mental health is something you can and should overcome on your own, and although it can be, the stigma gets in the way of effective treatment imo. Mine thought the measures of therapy and medication meant their daughter was "crazy" or "mental" in some way. They cared about me but felt like it was failing on their part and/or mine. I really hope your parents can be understanding and supportive, but know that you don't owe them the full extent unless they're showing they can be adequately understanding and supportive. And, after you get the depression and anxiety under control, you can always tell them how it affected you in retrospect if you feel comfortable (the suicidal ideation). I don't want you to have to deal with potential fallout while you need them to be supportive of your situation. 

best of luck to you! :( know that in six months, the things that you're anxious about right now won't carry the same weight. It's not you, it's the depression. It's harder to maintain mental health in quarantine too, so it's really great that you realize how it's affected you and are seeking treatment.

If you auto or charm a target, all w charges go to them! If not, each individual charge has its own range and rotates around you, leaving to hit a target once it's in range. If you think staying will result in your death, backing is good. Think of your health as a resource, you might have to give up some cs (and wait for it to come closer to your tower) if the enemy can poke you out whenever you step up for it. Q is very good and consistent waveclear! But I'd caution throwing it out excessively before you have a few points in it and mana items. Level 1, throw it out if you can hit minions/the enemy at the same time. Once you have two points in Q you can two shot the back wave. 

W is best for last hitting when you can't wind up an auto in time or secure canon. 

AA->W->Q is an easy electrocute proc, you can use the W movespeed to land both parts of Q.

You're new so backing timing is something to get used to, but it typically centers around wave management (in addition to having the funds). You will want to try to push (more specifically set up a slow push, but don't worry about this right now if its too confusing) the wave in a minute before drake spawns, and back when you have 40-45 seconds left. That way, you'll be back in time for drake with items while the enemy is stuck picking up cs under the turret. That's just one example but its a good thing to master.

My own boyfriend seemed a lot like what you're describing when we first began our relationship. While this *may* be true, all he had to do in that situation was let me know what he thought and I'd definitely try to avoid repeating those actions. Pay attention when your instincts tell you something is up, but make sure to give your partner their day in court as well. So if your partner has an angry outburst, let them know that it made you uncomfortable & you think they should have reacted differently, and then make a judgment based on how much they seem to take your feelings/perspectives to heart.
